frozen_evidence_boundary: useUndo call sites needed to establish undo availability
no issues, discussions, PRs or bug history before Phase B/C freeze
raw_signal_observation: Deleting a rule from MobileRuleEditPage requires an explicit confirmation and then exposes undo. Deleting a rule from MobileRulesPage directly sends rule-delete-all without confirmation and then exposes the same undo mechanism.
material_claim: Neta treated the sibling-path asymmetry as a violated destructive-action contract: the same entity and delete operation should use the same confirmation guard, so the list path was classified as a narrow local defect rather than an unresolved interaction-policy choice.
neta_next_move: Add the same confirmation guard to list-path rule deletion and pin the sibling consistency with a regression test; deliberately remove the guard as the positive control and require the test to turn red.
reversal_condition: If explicit product policy establishes that undo intentionally replaces confirmation in list context, revert the consistency change and route the policy to OWNER.
baseline_decision: BUILD: add a confirmation modal to list-path rule deletion for consistency with the edit path and to reduce accidental destructive actions.

evidence: Post-freeze issue #194 requested exactly a confirmation modal for rule deletion because of accidental-click risk; a maintainer initially called it a valid enhancement rather than a defect.
In the same issue, maintainer/developer j-f1 explicitly challenged the proposed confirmation: `I'm pretty sure undo works here, so maybe a confirmation isn't necessary?`

The issue was closed as a duplicate of a product discussion rather than as a repository invariant violation, while the pinned product still contains both confirmation+undo and undo-only rule-deletion paths.
adjudication.decision_delta: No advantage over baseline. Neta converted an inferred sibling-consistency preference into REPO-owned build permission even though the exact confirmation-versus-undo question was a product-policy tradeoff. The correct route was OWNER_DEFER or a policy discriminator.
adjudication.lesson: Equivalent-looking sibling paths do not establish a shared product contract. BUILD_READY from asymmetry is justified only when the invariant is explicit or otherwise independently established; inferred consistency can belong to OWNER.
